senses.gloss: m., du. מַחֲלָצַיִם, pl. מַחֲלָצִין (חָלַץ, cmp. חָלִיץ) a sort of windlass, loops of a rope attached to a heavy slab for rolling over plastered roofing &c., v. מַעֲגִילָה.
units: <cite ref="Makkot 9b:11">Macc. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>עד שישמט מַחֲלָצוֹ מידו</he> Var. in Ar. s. v. <cite ref="M00923"><he>מחצל</he></cite> (ed. <he>מחצלו</he>) until the entire ramming machine slips out of his hands (opp. to <cite ref="Q01350"><he>נפסק</he></cite> the breaking of the rope); Y. ib. II, beg. 31ᶜ <he>עד שיתיר את כל המחלצין</he> (read <he>שיפיל</he> or <he>שיוריד</he>) until he lets go all the loops (expl. = <he>נפסק החבל</he>). Ib. <he>מה דמר ר״י בשמיטת המ׳</he> (not <he>המחלצון</he>) what R. J. says (‘until he drops the whole rope’) refers to the slipping of the machine; Tosef. ib. II, 3 ed. Zuck. <he>עד שיפול כל המחצלין מידו</he> (read: <he>שיפיל … המחלצ׳</he>).

M. Kat. I, 10 (11ᵃ) שפין את … אבל לא במחלצים (Y. ed. … צַיִים; Ms. M. מחצלים) you may plaster over cracks in the roof, or roll them over with a (small) roller, using the hands or the feet, but not with the windlass, v. Y. ib. 81ᵃ top.—[The Var. lect. מחצל־ rests upon a popular transposition, as if from מָחַץ. The interpretation of מחצל by commentators as trowel does not fit the context.]
